headline: Former Prime Ministers Attend Ann Widdecombe Memorial In London
metaDescription: Former Prime Ministers and current political leaders gathered at Westminster Cathedral to attend the memorial service for late minister Ann Widdecombe.
aiSummaryBullets: Approximately 600 mourners attended the memorial service held at Westminster Cathedral.
Current Prime Minister Andy Burnham and former Prime Ministers David Cameron, Liz Truss, Boris Johnson, and Rishi Sunak were among the guests.
The Archbishop of Westminster was transported to a hospital for medical evaluation prior to the commencement of the service.
aiContextParagraph: A memorial service was held at Westminster Cathedral for former Conservative minister Ann Widdecombe, who was found deceased at her Devon home on July 9 at age 78. The event drew a significant number of political figures, with approximately 600 guests in attendance to pay their respects. Those present included current Prime Minister Andy Burnham, as well as former Prime Ministers David Cameron, Liz Truss, Boris Johnson, and Rishi Sunak. The service featured eulogies and a musical performance by the Westminster Cathedral choir. Proceedings were impacted earlier in the day when the Archbishop of Westminster, Richard Moth, was taken to a hospital for medical testing after becoming unwell. The gathering served as a moment for figures from across the political spectrum to honor the legacy of the late politician, who served as a prominent member of the Conservative Party during her long career.
whyItIsViral: The event is viral due to the high-profile attendance of multiple past and current British Prime Ministers, as reported by three independent news outlets with rapid coverage velocity.
